name: Shingles vaccine (recombinant zoster, RZV)
protects_against: Shingles (herpes zoster) and the long-term nerve pain it can cause

indications.reason: Two doses of the recombinant shingles vaccine are recommended for all adults aged 50 and older.
Adults aged 19 and older with a weakened immune system (from a condition or treatment) are recommended 2 doses of the recombinant shingles vaccine.

not_indicated_reason: The shingles vaccine is routinely recommended from age 50, or earlier for people with a weakened immune system.

series.note: The second dose is usually 2 to 6 months after the first. People with weakened immunity may be offered it 1 to 2 months after.

contraindications.text: A severe allergic reaction (such as anaphylaxis) after a previous dose, or to a vaccine ingredient.
Pregnancy. There is currently no recommendation for the shingles vaccine in pregnancy, and CDC suggests considering waiting until after pregnancy.

precautions.text: A moderate or severe illness right now, with or without fever.

content.disease: Shingles causes a painful skin rash, usually with blisters. It can lead to long-term nerve pain, called postherpetic neuralgia, which can last for months or years.
content.why: The risk of shingles and its complications rises with age and with a weakened immune system.
content.who: All adults aged 50 and older, and adults aged 19 and older with a weakened immune system.
content.doses_text: Two doses, usually 2 to 6 months apart.
content.catch_up: If more than 6 months have passed since your first dose, you don't need to restart. Get the second dose as soon as you can.
common_reactions: A sore arm with mild or moderate pain (very common)
Redness or swelling where the shot was given
content.reactions_duration: These usually go away on their own in 2 to 3 days.
serious_reactions: Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a serious nervous system disorder, has been reported very rarely after this vaccine.
A severe allergic reaction is very rare.
